swaps.name: Zoom
swaps.rewrite: Today I have Slack on my laptop, Zoom on my other laptop, and a Notion page explaining which one we actually use.
swaps.why: Zoom lands well and this room likes it 18% less than average—much better than Microsoft Teams at -27%. It ranks #2 in San Francisco and #1 in New York City. Works perfectly as another communication platform in the tool sprawl joke.

swaps.name: Asana
swaps.rewrite: Today I have Slack on my laptop, Asana on my other laptop, and a Notion page explaining which one we actually use.
swaps.why: Asana lands well and this room likes it 21% less than average, still beating Teams. It ranks #1 in San Francisco and #2 in New York City. Fits as a workplace tool that adds to the sprawl—teams often debate whether to chat in Slack or comment in Asana.

swaps.name: Grammarly
swaps.rewrite: Today I have Slack on my laptop, Grammarly on my other laptop, and a Notion page explaining which one we actually use.
swaps.why: Grammarly is the strongest fit: this room actually likes it 1% more than average. It lands well and ranks highly in both cities. While less obviously a communication tool, it works as another workplace productivity app that's always running, adding to the sense of digital clutter.

Microsoft Teams.note: All three options land better than Microsoft Teams with this room and fit the tool sprawl setup—Zoom is the most direct parallel as a communication platform, while Grammarly scores highest with the audience overall.

Kai Cenat.note: No substitute was confirmed for this room.
